rows: 1804 · Napoleon Crowned Emperor — 2 December 1804. Note: Napoleon placed the crown on his own head after Pius VII anointed him, though accounts of whether he took the crown from the pope's hands vary slightly.
1842 · Treaty of Nanking — 29 August 1842. [Claude at review: Extraterritoriality came in the 1843 supplementary treaty (Bogue), not Nanking itself.]

1853 · Commodore Perry Arrives in Japan — 8 July 1853 (first arrival at Uraga; Perry returned in February 1854 to sign the Convention of Kanagawa). Note that Japan maintained limited trade with the Dutch and Chinese at Nagasaki during sakoku, so avoid saying Japan was completely sealed off.
1861 · Battle of Fort Sumter — 12–13 April 1861. No soldiers were killed during the bombardment itself, though two Union soldiers died during the surrender salute.
1914 · Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand — 28 June 1914.
1915 · Gandhi Returns to India — 9 January 1915 (commemorated in India as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas).

1916 · Battle of the Somme — 1 July to 18 November 1916. Total casualties exceeded one million across all sides, including about 57,470 British casualties on 1 July alone. Tanks were used in combat for the first time during the battle in September 1916.

1917 · United States Enters World War I — 6 April 1917 (declared war on Austria-Hungary on 7 December 1917). [Claude at review: US troops played a modest part in stopping the spring offensives; their weight told later in 1918.]

1942 · Battle of Stalingrad — 23 August 1942 to 2 February 1943 (filed under 1942 as specified in the gap list). Total military and civilian casualties are estimated at around two million. [Claude at review: Germany counterattacked in early 1943 (Kharkov); the initiative passed for good after Kursk, July 1943.]
1942 · Battle of Midway — 4–7 June 1942. The US lost the carrier USS Yorktown, while Japan lost Akagi, Kaga, Soryu and Hiryu.
1945 · Germany Surrenders (V-E Day) — Act of surrender signed at Reims on 7 May 1945 and ratified in Berlin late on 8 May (early 9 May Moscow time, hence Victory Day on 9 May in Russia).
1953 · Korean Armistice Agreement — 27 July 1953. South Korea's Syngman Rhee refused to sign the agreement, and no formal peace treaty was ever concluded, leaving the two Koreas technically at war.

1975 · Apollo-Soyuz Test Project — Docking occurred on 17 July 1975 (mission ran 15–24 July 1975). Many historians treat it as the symbolic end of the Cold War Space Race. [Claude at review: A common reading, not a fact: our Space Race span ends with the Moon landing in 1969.]
1975 · Fall of Saigon — 30 April 1975. The city was renamed Ho Chi Minh City.
